correctness.rationale: For an involution with f singleton and m paired orbits, equivariance forces exactly f^f(f+2m)^m maps. A constant power must converge to one fixed-point root; rooted Cayley trees on fixed vertices contribute f^(f-1), and a weighted rooted forest on m paired orbits contributes f(f+2m)^(m-1). The Prüfer edge weights f to fixed sink and 2 to each other paired orbit give the latter exactly; product yields f^f N^(m-1), including f=1,m>=1, whereas m=0 gives f^(f-1). The n-ary table to X² swap-commuting transformations is bijective and preserves powers, yielding n^(n²-2). A separate direct enumerator counted all commuting maps for nine (f,m) values f=1..3,m=0..2 and agreed in each case, including 189/1323 for f=3,m=2. Finite tests corroborate, not establish the all-f,m proof.
